summary: This unit teaches you to take and process reservations at a villa or small property: finding what the guest wants, checking availability, quoting rates in US$ and J$, taking and confirming the booking, handling changes, cancellations, full-house requests and groups, and keeping the records and the guest's information safe.

blocks.p: This unit covers the work of the reservations desk at a villa or small property: answering a request, checking what is free, quoting the price, taking the booking, confirming it, changing or cancelling it, and keeping the records right. It is for HOSPITALITY VILLA/PROPERTIES SERVICES LEVEL 2 trainees. Every guest's stay begins with a reservation, so mistakes made here (a wrong date, a wrong price, a room sold twice) show up later at the front desk as angry guests and lost money.
A reservation is a **promise**. The guest promises to come and pay, and the property promises to keep a room or villa for them. Your job is to make that promise clear, correct and written down.

blocks.note: How you are assessed: two theory papers (multiple-choice questions, short answers and essays) and two practical tasks in the Centre's training room. In the practical tasks you take reservations by phone and email in role play, work out nights, rates and tax in US$ and J$, then process changes, cancellations and a group booking and prepare an arrivals list with the occupancy. The assessor watches your manner, your accuracy and your records.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.note: Use only made-up guest names, card numbers and contact details in practice. Shred or hand back all practice papers at the end of the session.
blocks.label: Tip

sections.title: Sources, room types and meal plans

blocks.p: Before you can take a reservation you must know where bookings come from, what you are selling and what is included in the price.

head: Source
What it is
What you record
rows: Direct
The guest phones, emails, uses the property's own website or comes to the desk
Contact details and how they found the property
Returning guest
A guest who has stayed before and books again
Past stay, likes and dislikes, any special rate
Travel agent or tour operator
An agent who books for their clients and is usually paid a commission
The agent's name and contact, the commission agreed, who pays the bill
Online travel agent (OTA)
A booking website that sells rooms for many properties
The booking reference, the rate and who collects payment
Corporate
A company that sends staff, often at an agreed corporate rate
Company name, the corporate rate, who pays
Walk-in
A guest who arrives with no booking and asks for a room
Treat like a new booking: check availability first

blocks.p: Always record the **source**. Managers use it to see which sources bring the most business and which cost the most in commission.

head: Type
Meaning
rows: Single
One bed for one person
Double
One large bed for two people
Twin
Two single beds in one room
Triple
A room for three people
Family room
A larger room for parents and children
Connecting rooms
Two rooms side by side with a door between them on the inside, often used by families
Suite
Separate living room and bedroom; usually the most costly room
Villa (whole-villa rental)
A private house with several bedrooms, a kitchen and often a pool; the whole villa is rented to one party

blocks.p: A guest alone in a double room is **single occupancy**, and some properties give it a separate rate. For a villa, find out the **number of bedrooms and the maximum number of guests**, and whether staff such as a cook, a housekeeper or a gardener are included in the price.

blocks.note: Views, floors and quiet rooms are usually requests, not promises. Write 'sea view requested' in the reservation and tell the guest it is not guaranteed unless the property's policy says it is.
blocks.label: Tip

head: Letters
Name
What is included
rows: EP
European Plan
Room only, no meals
CP
Continental Plan
Room and a continental breakfast
BP

Room and a full breakfast
MAP
Modified American Plan
Room, breakfast and dinner
AP (FAP)
American Plan (Full American Plan)

blocks.p: Say the plan every time you quote a price. A guest who thinks breakfast is included, when it is not, will feel cheated at check-out.

Demand changes through the year. **High season** is the busiest time, when rates are highest; in Jamaica it usually runs from about mid-December to April, but follow your property's own calendar. **Low season** has lower rates. Some properties set a **minimum stay**, for example 5 nights at Christmas. The **rack rate** is the full, standard price before any discount. A **corporate rate**, a **package** or a **special offer** is lower and has conditions.

blocks.note: Only the manager, or the person the policy names, can approve a discount or a special rate. If a guest asks for one, say politely that you will check and come back to them.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.p: Many Jamaican villas and hotels price in **US$** because most guests come from overseas. Local guests may want J$. Guests also ask 'Is tax included?' Quote clearly and put the answer in writing.

ul: The room or villa type and the number of guests it covers
Whether the rate is **per room, per villa or per person**, and **per night**
The meal plan included
The currency (US$ or J$)
Whether **GCT** (General Consumption Tax) and any **service charge** are included or added, at the current rates
Any extra charges, such as a cleaning fee, an extra-person charge or a resort fee
The deposit, how and when to pay it, and the cancellation terms

blocks.p: The number of nights is the departure date minus the arrival date. A guest who arrives on 12 December and leaves on 15 December stays **3 nights**: you count the nights slept, not the days.

ol: Count the nights (departure date minus arrival date)
Multiply the nightly rate by the number of nights
Add extras, such as an extra person or a cleaning fee
Add the service charge if it is added to the rate
Add GCT on the right amount, at the current rate
Convert to J$ only if the guest asks, using the property's rate for that day

blocks.p: **Worked example (made-up figures for practice only).** A villa rate is US$300 a night for 4 nights, with a cleaning fee of US$60. A service charge of 10% and tax of 15% are added. Always use the property's real, current rates.

head: Step
Sum
Result
rows: Room cost
US$300 x 4 nights
Add cleaning fee
Service charge (10%, made up)
Subtotal
Tax (15%, made up)
Total in US$

blocks.p: If the property's exchange rate that day is made-up US$1 = J$155, the total in J$ is 1,593.90 x 155 = J$247,054.50. The guest should be told that the J$ figure can change when the property's rate changes.

blocks.note: The order in which tax and service charge are added differs between properties. Follow the property's rate sheet and ask your supervisor. Work every sum twice, or have a colleague check it.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.note: Guests from overseas may know the price from a website or from an agent. If your quotation is different, check which is the current rate and explain politely. Never argue with the guest; ask the manager.
blocks.label: Jamaica

sections.title: Taking a reservation by phone and by email

blocks.p: Answer within a few rings. Smile; guests can hear it. **Greet the caller, name the property and give your name**: 'Good morning, Sunrise Villa reservations, Andre speaking. How may I help you?' Speak clearly and slowly, and keep a pen and the reservation form or the screen ready. If you need to look something up, say 'May I put you on hold for a moment?' and wait for the answer.

flow: Find dates, number of guests, room type
Give the confirmation number and thank the caller

blocks.p: Ask for the **dates, the number of guests (adults and children) and the room or villa type**. Do not ask for personal details until you know you have something to sell.

ul: Say dates in words with the day of the week: 'Saturday, 12 December'.
Check arrival and departure dates, and say the **number of nights**.

Guests from the USA often write the month first, so 03/04 may mean 4 March, not 3 April. In Jamaica and Europe the day usually comes first. **Always check the date with the guest and write the month in words.**
Use the 24-hour clock for times if the property does, for example 15:00 for 3 p.m.

head: Detail
Why it matters
rows: Full name of the guest who will stay (as on the passport)
To find the booking and to greet the guest
Booker's name, if different
The person who booked and pays may not be the guest
Dates, nights, room type, number of adults and children
What was agreed, and the charge
Rate, meal plan and currency
So the price is clear to both sides
Phone number, email address and home address
To contact the guest and send the confirmation
Guarantee or deposit, and cancellation terms
To protect the property from a no-show
Estimated time of arrival (ETA) and flight details
So the room, the transfer and the cook are ready
Special requests: cot, diet, birthday, access needs
So departments can prepare
Source of the booking and your own name
For reports, and in case of a query

blocks.note: If the guest and the person booking are different (for example Mrs Clarke books for her son), the **guest's name goes on the reservation**, with the booker noted.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.p: Ask the caller to spell the surname, then spell it back using clear words, for example M for Mike, A for Alpha. Check unusual names twice. A wrong spelling means the booking cannot be found at check-in.

ul: Reply **promptly**, within the time the property sets (often within a few hours, and always the same day).
Use a polite greeting, the guest's name and a clear answer to every question.
State the dates, nights, room type, rate, meal plan, taxes, deposit and cancellation terms.
Ask for anything missing, for example the number of guests or the arrival time.
Read the request again before you send the reply. Check spelling and figures.
Never ask guests to send full card numbers by ordinary email. Give them the property's safe payment method.

blocks.p: Before saving a new reservation, check every detail against your notes. Then update the chart or system **at once**. A booking that is only on a scrap of paper is a booking waiting to be lost.

blocks.note: A guest's information belongs to the guest. Ask only for what the property needs. Never confirm to another caller whether a person is staying. Say, 'I cannot give out guest information, but I can take a message.'
blocks.label: Safety

head: Point
Guaranteed
Non-guaranteed
rows: How it is secured
By a credit card, a deposit paid or a written agreement (for example a company guarantee)
No payment; only a promise to arrive
How long the room is held
All night, even if the guest arrives very late
Only until the **release time**, such as 6 p.m.
If the guest does not arrive
A no-show charge may be made under the policy
The room is released and may be sold to someone else
Best for
Busy periods, villas and high season
Quiet periods, and walk-in style demand

blocks.p: A **deposit** holds the booking and covers the property if the guest does not arrive or cancels late. Villas often ask for a deposit when the booking is made, a second payment before arrival and the balance on arrival or departure. Some also take a **security (damage) deposit**, which is returned if there is no damage. Explain how much, when it is due, and what happens to it if the guest cancels.

blocks.note: Card details are given only to guarantee or pay for the booking. Type them straight into the secure system. Never write them on paper, read them aloud where others can hear, or leave them in an open email. Do not keep the card security code (the three or four extra digits) after the payment has been authorised. Follow your property's policy.
blocks.label: Safety

blocks.p: **Read the booking back to the caller** so that any mistake is found now and not at check-in. Then give a **confirmation number**: the guest quotes it if they call again, and you can find the booking at once. Send a written confirmation by email or letter.

head: A confirmation shows
Example
rows: Guest name and booker
Mr Delroy Spence
Dates and nights
Arrive Friday 6 March, depart Tuesday 10 March, 4 nights
Room or villa, guests, meal plan
Two-bedroom villa, 4 adults, EP
Rate, currency, taxes and extras
US$ per night, GCT and service charge stated
Deposit paid and balance due
Deposit received; balance due on arrival
Cancellation and no-show terms
Free cancellation up to a set date
Check-in and check-out times, property contacts and directions
Check-in from 15:00; check-out by 11:00
Confirmation number
Quote it in all contact with us

blocks.p: Check-in and check-out times differ between properties: often check-in is from about 2 or 3 p.m. and check-out is about 11 a.m. or noon. Use your property's times.

sections.title: Changes, cancellations, full house and no-shows

flow: Find the booking by name and confirmation number
Check the caller is the guest or booker
Check availability for the new details
Explain any change in rate, fee or deposit
Update the booking and tell departments
Read back and send a new confirmation

blocks.p: **Check availability first**. Never agree to a new date before you know the room is free for every night. If the new dates are not free, offer other dates or another room type.

ol: Find and check the booking with the guest
Refer any exception (such as illness or a hurricane warning) to the supervisor
Cancel in the system and give a **cancellation number**
Record the date, time, reason, refund or charge and your name
Release the room and offer it to the waiting list

blocks.p: If the policy says the deposit is lost for cancellations within 7 days, and a guest cancels two days before arrival, explain the policy politely and follow it. Do not make exceptions yourself.

blocks.note: Weather can change plans. When a hurricane or a storm warning is in force, the manager may relax the rules for guests who cannot travel. Refer these calls to the supervisor and record what was agreed.
blocks.label: Jamaica

ul: Say sorry politely and clearly.
Offer **other dates or another room type**.
Offer the **waiting list** and explain that it is not a promise.
Suggest another property if the policy allows.
Record the request (a 'turn-away') and thank the caller.

blocks.p: Keep a **waiting list** with the name, phone number, dates and room type. When a cancellation comes in, call the first guest on the list quickly.

A **no-show** is a guest who books but does not arrive and does not cancel. The room could have been sold, so the property loses money. To reduce no-shows: ask for a guarantee or deposit, explain the terms, **reconfirm** by phone or email a few days before arrival, and release non-guaranteed rooms at the release time.

**Overbooking** is taking more bookings than there are rooms. Some properties do it on purpose, because some guests do not come. If everyone arrives, someone has no room. The property must then **walk** the guest: pay for a room at another property, and bring the guest back as soon as it can. Guests with a guaranteed booking are looked after first. The manager arranges this, not the reservations agent.

blocks.note: Never promise a room you have not checked. If you are not sure, say, 'Let me check and call you back within the hour.'
blocks.label: Remember

sections.title: Group bookings, special requests and selling

blocks.p: A group can be a wedding party, a family reunion, a church retreat or a sports team. Groups bring many room nights, so they are valuable, but they need careful work.

flow: Take the organiser's details, dates, rooms and who pays
Check availability and agree the group rate with the manager
Block the rooms with a cut-off date
Send a written contract or confirmation
Enter the names and tell the departments

head: Term
Meaning
rows: Block or allotment
Rooms held for a group or an agent until a set date
Cut-off date
The date after which unsold rooms in the block go back on sale
Rooming list
The list of guests in the group with who shares each room, and arrival and departure dates
Master account
One bill for the items the organiser pays, with other items paid by each guest
Group rate
A reduced rate agreed for the group

blocks.p: Ask the organiser who pays for what (rooms, meals, drinks, activities). Say what happens if fewer rooms are used than were blocked. Pass special needs, such as late arrivals, a welcome drink, diets and a wedding setup, to the other departments in good time.

Write requests in the reservation, as special requests: a baby cot, a sea view, a late arrival, a birthday cake, an extra bed, diet or access needs. Do not promise what the policy does not allow. Tell housekeeping, the kitchen and the front desk.

**Upselling** means offering something better or extra that suits the guest. Good upselling listens first. A couple booking an anniversary stay may like a room with a private plunge pool, a dinner package or a spa treatment. A family may like a villa with a cook. Describe the benefit, state the price clearly and accept 'no' with a smile. Never push, and never say something is included when it is not.

head: Good selling
Poor selling
rows: Asks about the occasion and the budget first
Offers the most expensive room to everyone
Describes how it helps the guest
Uses pressure or says "only one left" when it is not true
States the extra cost clearly
Hides charges until check-out
Accepts the guest's choice
Argues or sulks if the guest says no

blocks.p: If a caller is angry because the property is full, stay calm. Listen, say sorry, do not blame anyone, and offer choices (other dates, other room types, the waiting list). Never raise your voice. If the caller will not calm down, ask your supervisor to take the call.

blocks.note: Local guests and guests from overseas may like the same things. Do not guess a guest's budget from their accent, their clothes or their name.
blocks.label: Jamaica

blocks.h: The reservation chart and the PMS

blocks.p: A **reservation chart** shows which rooms are booked for each night, on paper. A **property management system (PMS)** does this on a computer. Whichever you use, it must be **up to date** so that rooms are not double-booked or left empty. Enter every booking, change and cancellation at once. Check twice before you save.

head: Report
Shows
Used by
rows: Arrivals list
The guests due to arrive on a given day, with room, ETA and requests
Front desk, housekeeping, bell staff, kitchen
Departures list
The guests due to leave on a given day
Front desk, housekeeping, bell staff
In-house list
Everyone staying tonight
Front desk and security, and used in an emergency
Waiting list
Guests who want dates that are full
Reservations

blocks.p: **Occupancy** is the share of the rooms that are sold. Occupancy per cent = rooms sold divided by rooms available, times 100.

Example: a villa property has 20 rooms and 15 are booked tonight. 15 divided by 20 = 0.75, and 0.75 x 100 = **75%**. Another night 9 of 12 are sold: 9 divided by 12 = 0.75, which is also 75%. Do not count rooms that are out of order as available if the property's policy excludes them.

blocks.note: Managers use occupancy, past no-show records and the booking source to decide the rates, the staff needed and how many rooms, if any, to overbook.
blocks.label: Remember

ul: Never tell a caller or visitor whether someone is staying, their dates or their room. Offer to take a message, or to put the call through.
Ask only for the information the property needs.
Card details go only into the secure system, never on paper or into open email.
Use your own password, never share it, and lock the screen when you leave the desk.
Keep printed lists such as arrivals lists out of sight and **shred** them when no longer needed.
Do not talk about guests in public areas, on your phone or on social media.

blocks.p: Jamaica's data protection law requires organisations to look after personal information and to use it only for the purpose it was given. Your supervisor will tell you the property's rules.

blocks.note: If you see something wrong in the system, such as a double booking, tell your supervisor at once. Do not hide it or fix it in secret.
blocks.label: Tip

c1.title: A phone enquiry for a villa in Negril
c1.text: Mrs Marcia Henry phones Palm Breeze Villa in Negril. She wants to book for her husband Lloyd, their daughter and her 3-year-old son, from Friday 20 March to Tuesday 24 March. The villa has two bedrooms, each with one double bed, and a cook can be added. The rate is EP at US$280 a night for the whole villa, with a one-off cleaning fee of US$50. Mrs Henry asks what the price is in J$. For this exercise the property's exchange rate for the day is made up as US$1 = J$156. She says she will pay a deposit by card.

c2.title: An email from Canada
c2.text: Reservations at Blue Hole Guest Cottages receive an email from Mr Daniel Roy of Toronto asking for a double room for 'arrival 06/07, 5 nights'. He asks whether breakfast is included and whether his friend Mr Anil Dass, who is arriving the same day, can have the room next door. He also asks the receptionist to confirm the room number his friend has already booked. The property has CP and EP rates, and the email arrived on a Sunday evening.

c3.title: A cancellation and a no-show in Ocho Rios
c3.text: At Seaview Lodge in Ocho Rios the cancellation policy says the first night's rate is charged for cancellations less than 7 days before arrival. Ms Keisha Bryan phones to cancel a three-night booking for Saturday, which is 4 days away; she has a guaranteed booking with her card. The same night, two non-guaranteed bookings have a release time of 6 p.m. and neither guest has arrived or called by 6:15 p.m. A caller on the waiting list is waiting for Saturday.

c4.title: A family reunion in Treasure Beach
c4.text: Mr Orville Ellis phones a villa property in Treasure Beach to arrange a family reunion for 7 rooms from Friday to Monday. The property has 10 rooms. He wants the best group rate, will pay for rooms only, and says guests will pay their own meals. He says the final names will be sent 'closer to the time'. The manager has approved a group rate and a cut-off date 21 days before arrival.

c5.title: A busy reservations desk in Montego Bay
c5.text: The reservations desk at a villa property in Montego Bay has 12 rooms. Tonight 9 rooms are booked. A caller, Mrs Cooper, wants the villa's last room for two weekends in December but all rooms are taken for one of them, and she gets angry. The desk also gets a caller who says, 'Is my friend Mr Grant staying with you?' The agent, Shanice, knows the reservation system is slow and the date on screen may be wrong.

questions.q: Mrs Henry's guests arrive on Friday 20 March and leave on Tuesday 24 March. How many nights is that?
o: 4 nights
5 nights
3 nights
6 nights
questions.why: The nights are the nights slept: 20, 21, 22 and 23 March. Departure date minus arrival date is 24 - 20 = 4.

questions.q: What is the cost of the room and the cleaning fee in US$, before any tax or service charge?
questions.why: 4 nights x US$280 = US$1,120, plus the one-off cleaning fee of US$50 = US$1,170.

questions.q: Mrs Henry asks for the US$1,170 in J$. What should the agent do?
o: Use the rate shown on a bank website, because the bank sets the market rate
Round the US$ price to a figure that is easy for the guest to remember
Use the property's rate for the day and say the J$ figure may change
Say that only US$ is accepted and refuse to give any J$ price at all
questions.why: The property sets its own exchange rate each day: 1,170 x 156 = J$182,520. Tell the guest the J$ figure depends on that day's rate.

questions.q: The agent quotes the price but forgets to say 'EP'. Why does this matter?
o: EP means dinner is included, so the kitchen must be told to prepare it
EP decides the time at which a non-guaranteed room is released
EP is only needed when the guest pays the deposit by card
EP is room only, so a guest expecting breakfast will be surprised
questions.why: EP is the European Plan: room only. If the plan is not stated, the guest may think meals are included and feel cheated later.

questions.q: Mr Roy writes 'arrival 06/07, 5 nights'. What should the agent do about the date?
o: Ask him to confirm it in words, as it may be 7 June or 6 July
Take it as 6 July, since Jamaica and Europe write the day first
Take it as 7 June, since the guest lives in North America and writes the month first
Choose whichever of the two possible dates has a room free for 5 nights
questions.why: Date order differs between countries. Check the date in words, for example 'Monday 6 July', so the booking is on the right nights.

questions.q: Mr Roy asks the receptionist to confirm the room his friend Mr Dass has booked. What is the correct reply?
o: Tell him the room number, since the two men are friends and are travelling together
Say it cannot give out guest information, and offer to pass on a message
Say that Mr Dass has no booking, so that nothing about him is ever revealed
Give only the floor and not the room number, as a safe compromise to the guest
questions.why: Guest information is private. Never confirm or deny that someone is staying; offer to take a message. A floor number also gives away information.

questions.q: When should the property reply to Mr Roy's email, sent on Sunday evening?
o: On Friday, when the manager has time to read all of the week's mail
After he phones to ask why he has had no answer from the property yet
Promptly, within the property's set time, with the rate, meal plan and terms
Within a month, because email is not as urgent as a telephone call or visit
questions.why: Email requests should be answered promptly, within the property's set time. A late answer often means the guest books somewhere else.

questions.q: Mr Roy offers to send his credit card number in his next email. What should the agent do?
o: Accept it, then copy the number onto a card kept in the locked desk drawer
Accept it and save the whole email in the booking folder for later use
Ask him to send only the first twelve digits and give the rest by phone
Ask him to use the property's secure payment method, not ordinary email
questions.why: Plain email can be read by others. Follow the property's policy: use the secure system or payment link, and delete any card number that arrives by email.

questions.q: Ms Bryan cancels 4 days before arrival. The policy charges the first night inside 7 days. What should the agent do first?
o: Find the booking and explain the policy politely before cancelling
Cancel it and waive the charge, to keep the guest happy with the villa
Ask her to phone back later, when the manager is in the office to decide
Explain that only a cancellation made in writing can ever be charged
questions.why: Find and check the booking, and explain the policy before you cancel. The agent follows the policy and refers any request for an exception to the supervisor.

questions.q: After cancelling the booking, what should the agent give Ms Bryan?
o: A new confirmation number for dates later in the same year
A cancellation number and a written notice
A discount voucher to use on her next stay at the property
Nothing more, as the booking has now been removed from the system
questions.why: A cancellation number is proof of when the booking was cancelled. Send a written notice, and record the date, time, reason and any charge.

questions.q: What should happen to Ms Bryan's room after the cancellation?
o: It stays blocked in her name until the Saturday has arrived
It is sold at once to the first walk-in guest who comes to the desk
It is released and offered first to the waiting-list caller
It is kept empty until the housekeeper has checked the whole villa
questions.why: A cancelled room goes back on sale at once. A waiting list lets the property resell it quickly, starting with the first guest who asked.

questions.q: At 6:15 p.m. the two non-guaranteed guests have not arrived or called. The release time was 6 p.m. What may the property do?
o: Hold the rooms until midnight in case the guests come
Charge each guest a no-show fee on their card
Phone each guest and ask for a deposit before releasing
Release the rooms and sell them to other guests
questions.why: A non-guaranteed booking is held only until the release time. With no card or deposit, there is nothing to charge, so the rooms may be resold.

questions.q: Mr Ellis asks for 7 rooms for a family reunion. What should the agent do first?
o: Check availability and agree the group rate with the manager
Block all 10 rooms to be safe, then tell the manager at the end
Send the rooming list form to the housekeeper to fill in first
Quote the rack rate and take a deposit without any further checks
questions.why: Check that the rooms are free and agree the rate with the manager before promising anything. Groups need an approved rate and clear terms.

questions.q: What does a cut-off date of 21 days before arrival mean for the group?
o: The group must pay the full bill on that date at the desk
Rooms in the block not confirmed by then go back on sale
No guest may change rooms after that date has passed
The property stops taking any new bookings from that date
questions.why: The cut-off date is when unused rooms in the block are released. It protects the property from holding rooms that may never be used.

questions.q: Mr Ellis says the guests' names will come 'closer to the time'. What should the agent do?
o: Wait, and let the guests give their names when they reach the front desk
Enter each room as 'Guest 1', 'Guest 2' and keep those names until arrival
Agree a date for the rooming list before cut-off and confirm it in writing
Tell him names are not needed at all because the block is already held
questions.why: A rooming list names each guest and who shares a room, so staff can prepare. Agree a date, and put it in the written confirmation.

questions.q: Mr Ellis will pay for rooms only. How should the other costs be handled?
o: Put every guest's extras on the first guest's bill to keep things simple
Treat all extras as free, because the group has a special rate
Ask each guest to pay in cash at the end of each day
Record who pays for what, so meals and drinks go on each guest's own bill
questions.why: A group can have a master account for what the organiser pays and separate bills for personal items. Write the payment rules in the confirmation.

questions.q: With 9 of the 12 rooms sold tonight, what share of the rooms is still unsold?
questions.why: Occupancy is rooms sold divided by rooms available x 100: 9 divided by 12 = 75%. The unsold share is the rest, 100 - 75 = 25%, which is 3 rooms.

questions.q: Mrs Cooper is angry that one weekend is full. What should Shanice do?
o: Tell her that the property always has rooms free on all of the other weekends
Stay calm, say sorry, and offer other dates, a room type or the waiting list
Promise the weekend she wants and sort out the problem with the guests later
Ask the cook to explain to her why the weekend cannot be booked
questions.why: Stay calm and offer real choices. Never promise a room you do not have, and explain that the waiting list is not a promise.

questions.q: Shanice thinks the screen shows the wrong date. What should she do before saving the booking?
o: Save it now and correct the date when the guest arrives at the front desk
Ask the guest to type the booking into the system by herself, to be sure
Check every detail against her notes, then report the fault
Leave the booking out of the system until the following day, to be safe
questions.why: Check every detail against your notes before saving, and report the fault to your supervisor. A wrong date means a missing room or a double booking.

questions.q: Which step helps most to reduce no-shows?
o: Overbooking by as many rooms as the property can afford to lose each night
Sending no reminders at all, so that guests are not annoyed or worried
Taking bookings without a contact number, to keep each call short
Asking for a guarantee or deposit, and reconfirming before arrival
questions.why: A guarantee or deposit, clear terms and a reminder before arrival make guests more likely to arrive or to cancel in time.
